name: Kimura Switch
summary: A Kimura switch requires wrist control and a figure-four arm grip around the elbow; an Aoki rotational foot grip must be released before a separate arm capture.
description: A Kimura switch requires wrist control and a figure-four arm grip around the elbow; an Aoki rotational foot grip must be released before a separate arm capture.
overview:
The initial Aoki Lock Control configuration must be identified before considering Kimura Trap. The captured limb is the foot and lower leg. This is distinct from an omoplata-style shoulder trap and from a bent-knee calf slicer. Either player can become the foot-lock attacker during an entanglement exchange. The reviewed instruction does not establish a direct Aoki Lock Control-to-Kimura Trap connection. Release the original lock safely and establish the destination's own prerequisites; do not treat these checkpoints as a demonstrated continuous entry.

The opposing foot is turned outward and enclosed near the armpit, upper arm, and forearm. Rotational foot locks can injure the ankle or knee before pain provides useful warning. Use cooperative capture-and-release practice, no spinning escapes, and the event's actual division rules. Open the original connection before either partner turns, rises or changes the captured limb.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Stephan Kesting and Rob Biernacki — the Aoki lock](https://www.grapplearts.com/the-step-by-step-aoki-lock/); [IBJJF — current rule resources](https://ibjjf.com/books-videos).

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (attacker): What is held in the initial Aoki configuration?
flashcards.answer: The opposing foot is turned outward and enclosed near the armpit, upper arm, and forearm.
flashcards.answer_line: An outward-turned foot beside the armpit

plausible: An inward-turned foot beside the armpit
A straight ankle with the instep outside the upper arm
trap: An outward heel with the forefoot outside both arms

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (attacker): Why unload the first capture before reaching for an arm?
flashcards.answer: Rotational foot locks can injure the ankle or knee before pain provides useful warning. Use cooperative capture-and-release practice, no spinning escapes, and the event's actual division rules.
flashcards.answer_line: Body movement can rotate the restrained foot and knee

plausible: The foot enclosure unloads as soon as one hand reaches for the wrist
Hip movement transfers force into calf muscle without rotating the knee
trap: The lower-leg grip can stay loaded if the new wrist grip is secure

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (attacker): What must open before the target limb changes?
flashcards.answer: Open the original connection before either partner turns, rises or changes the captured limb.
flashcards.answer_line: The foot enclosure and its hip connection

plausible: Only the hand reaching for the new wrist
Only the leg on the hip, keeping the instep clamped
trap: Only the heel support, keeping the hip and upper arm tight

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (attacker): What access is needed for the new kimura grip?
flashcards.answer: Obtain a separate arm-control position before attempting a figure-four grip.
flashcards.answer_line: The opponent's wrist and elbow from an arm-control position

plausible: Their wrist with the elbow hidden tight behind the torso
Their elbow while their wrist stays out of reach
trap: Their hand alone with your second arm outside the elbow

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (attacker): How is the arm figure-four connected?
flashcards.answer: Hold the opposing wrist and your own wrist while keeping the captured elbow controlled.
flashcards.answer_line: Hold their wrist and your own wrist around their arm

plausible: Hold their wrist with both hands side by side
Hold your own wrist with both arms outside their elbow
trap: Hold their wrist and upper arm with unconnected hands

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (attacker): In a positional kimura drill, what is the intended endpoint?
flashcards.answer: Use the grip as a positional handle without forcing the wrist behind the back.
flashcards.answer_line: Secure wrist-and-elbow control without forcing the shoulder

plausible: Move the wrist behind the back to confirm shoulder pressure
Keep the wrist but release the wrap to let the elbow travel
trap: Use torso rotation to test whether the shoulder can follow

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (attacker): Which lower-body connection belongs to the initial setup?
flashcards.answer: The initial Aoki setup manages foot and hip; those lower-body controls are dismantled before arm capture.
flashcards.answer_line: A leg attachment managing the captured foot's hip

plausible: A grip on the foot with both legs outside the hip
A knee touching the thigh while the hip moves freely
trap: Both ankles crossed without enclosing the opposing leg

flashcards.answer: The captured limb is the foot and lower leg. This is distinct from an omoplata-style shoulder trap and from a bent-knee calf slicer. Release the original lock safely and establish the destination's own prerequisites; do not treat these checkpoints as a demonstrated continuous entry.
flashcards.answer_line: It encloses a foot rather than controlling wrist and elbow

plausible: The same upper-arm grip already surrounds the opposing elbow
A palm-to-palm foot grip supplies the required self-wrist connection
trap: The foot enclosure restrains the shoulder through the shared grip shape

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (attacker): Your partner turns while the wrist and shoulder remain fixed. What next?
flashcards.answer: Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.
flashcards.answer_line: Release the arm restraint before allowing the turn

plausible: Open the wrist grip but leave the elbow wrap wedged
Turn with the partner before releasing the figure-four
trap: Relax the hand pressure while keeping the wrist fixed

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (attacker): With one hand on their wrist, how does the other complete the figure-four?
flashcards.answer: Keep the first hand on the opposing wrist. The second arm wraps around their elbow and connects to your own wrist, securing the figure-four before any shoulder pressure.
flashcards.answer_line: Circle their elbow and take your own wrist

plausible: Place the second hand beside the first on their wrist
Wrap their forearm without passing around the elbow
trap: Grip their upper arm with the second hand and release the wrist

defender.description: Kimura Switch (defender): Hold the arm close to the torso before a figure-four grip closes. Recover inside arm position while the attacker has only one point of control.
defender.overview:
The initial Aoki Lock Control configuration must be identified before considering Kimura Trap. The captured limb is the foot and lower leg. This is distinct from an omoplata-style shoulder trap and from a bent-knee calf slicer. Either player can become the foot-lock attacker during an entanglement exchange. The reviewed instruction does not establish a direct Aoki Lock Control-to-Kimura Trap connection. Release the original lock safely and establish the destination's own prerequisites; do not treat these checkpoints as a demonstrated continuous entry.

Hold the arm close to the torso before a figure-four grip closes. Recover inside arm position while the attacker has only one point of control. A Kimura threatens the shoulder and elbow, unlike the preceding foot lock.

Do not roll against a fixed wrist and shoulder. Stop before the arm is driven behind the back. Recover posture and facing frames after the arm grip opens.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

The early escape keeps the wrist near the torso and denies the elbow wrap while only one grip is present. If the arm has been released and you remain underneath, use a short hip escape behind a frame to face the opponent. This guard retention keeps the returning knee between the bodies before the opponent can advance.

Avoid a forced roll: Do not roll against a fixed wrist and shoulder.
Tap before shoulder loading: Stop before the arm is driven behind the back.
Reset once released: Recover posture and facing frames after the arm grip opens.

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (defender): Before the figure-four closes, where should you keep the arm?
flashcards.answer: Hold the arm close to the torso before a figure-four grip closes.
flashcards.answer_line: Wrist and elbow close to the torso

plausible: Wrist extended far behind your shoulder
Elbow flared while the hand reaches across their back
trap: Hand on the floor with the shoulder turned away

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (defender): With only your wrist held, how do you deny the next grip?
flashcards.answer: Recover inside arm position while the attacker has only one point of control.
flashcards.answer_line: Recover inside arm position before the elbow wrap

plausible: Extend the elbow farther beyond their shoulder
Turn the torso away while leaving the wrist fixed
trap: Wait for both grips to close before hand fighting

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (defender): Which limb relationship signals the new threat after Aoki release?
flashcards.answer: A Kimura threatens the shoulder and elbow, unlike the preceding foot lock.

plausible: Two hands holding your wrist with your elbow free
An elbow held while your wrist can withdraw freely
trap: A forearm wrap leaving the elbow outside

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (defender): Why should you not roll with the wrist and shoulder fixed?
flashcards.answer: Do not roll against a fixed wrist and shoulder. Create slack in the existing control before changing the body angle.
flashcards.answer_line: Your torso can rotate against the isolated shoulder

plausible: The wrist grip slides free before the shoulder follows the torso
The retained elbow wrap lets the upper arm rotate with the chest
trap: The forearm absorbs the turn without transmitting load to the shoulder

flashcards.question: Kimura Switch (defender): What should end a cooperative positional hold?
flashcards.answer: Stop before the arm is driven behind the back. Create slack in the existing control before changing the body angle.
flashcards.answer_line: Capture before the wrist is driven behind the back

plausible: A small wrist lift to check shoulder resistance
A turn that proves the elbow cannot escape
trap: A hand reaching the spine while the elbow stays held
